title: A sample's warp map survives a round trip through .alc and .asd
description:
## Behavior
A sample's warp map written as a sidecar and read back is the same warp map. `.asd` rows apply only if M0 says **go**.

```gherkin
Feature: Warp map round trip
  A warp map written as a DAW sidecar and read back is unchanged, pickups and mid-bar tempo changes included.

  Scenario Outline: A steady sample round-trips
    Given the fixture sample "steady-120.wav" and its analysis
    When I write its warp map as <format>
    And I read that <format> back
    Then the warp markers match the analysis to within 0.1 ms and 0.001 beats
    And the warp mode is "complex"
    And the detune matches the sample's tuning correction

    Examples:
      | format |
      | .alc   |
      | .asd   |

  Scenario: Pickup beats keep their negative numbers
    Given the fixture sample "steady-120.wav" whose first beat is a pickup at beat -1
    When I write its warp map as .alc and read it back
    Then the first warp marker is at beat -1
    And beat 0 is still the first downbeat

  Scenario: A tempo change in the middle of a bar survives
    Given the fixture sample "tempo-change.wav" with a warp marker at beat 6.5
    When I write its warp map as .alc and read it back
    Then there is a warp marker at beat 6.5 at the same second

  Scenario: A sample without a beat grid is written unwarped
    Given the fixture sample "free-time.wav" whose analysis found no beat grid
    When I write its warp map as .alc and read it back
    Then warping is off and there are no warp markers
```
